title: PostgreSQL connection pool exhausted
symptoms: Connection timeouts on /api/login, HTTP 500 errors, DB max_connections reached
root_cause: Missing connection.close() in retry loop introduced in v2.3.1 deployment
investigation_steps: Checked error logs — saw too many connections errors starting at 02:03
Checked DB metrics — active connections at 100/100 max_connections limit
Reviewed recent deployments — auth-service v2.3.1 deployed at 01:47
Diffed v2.3.1 vs v2.3.0 — found missing connection.close() in error handler
resolution_steps: Run: SELECT count(*), state FROM pg_stat_activity GROUP BY state to confirm connections maxed
Run: git diff v2.3.0..v2.3.1 to find the connection leak
Rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/auth-service
Monitor: watch connection count drop below 20 within 5 minutes

title: Payment service high latency — Redis cache miss storm
symptoms: Payment processing taking 8-12 seconds instead of normal 200ms, checkout timeouts
root_cause: Redis cache flushed during scheduled maintenance, all requests hitting DB directly
investigation_steps: Checked payment-service logs — slow DB queries on every request
Checked Redis metrics — cache hit rate dropped from 94% to 2%
Found scheduled maintenance task flushed Redis at 03:00
DB query time was normal but volume was 50x higher than usual
resolution_steps: Check Redis cache hit rate: redis-cli INFO stats | grep keyspace_hits
Confirm maintenance job ran: check cron logs at /var/log/maintenance.log
Manually warm cache by running: python scripts/warm_cache.py
Monitor hit rate recovery — should return to 90%+ within 15 minutes

title: Notification service memory leak — OOM crash loop
symptoms: notification-service pod restarting every 20 mins, OOMKilled in events
root_cause: Email template renderer accumulating parsed templates in memory without eviction
investigation_steps: Checked service logs — OOMKilled events every 18-22 minutes
Checked memory metrics — steady linear increase before each crash
Heap dump showed 85% memory held by template cache objects
Traced to template_renderer.py — cache had no max size or TTL set
resolution_steps: Confirm memory pattern: kubectl top pod -l app=notification-service --containers
Check template cache size in logs: grep 'template_cache size' /var/log/notification.log
Immediate relief: kubectl rollout restart deployment/notification-service
Permanent fix: add LRU cache with max_size=100 and TTL=3600 in template_renderer.py
Deploy fix and verify memory stays flat over 30 minutes

title: API gateway 503 — upstream timeout to inventory service
symptoms: All product listing pages showing errors, 503 from API gateway logs
root_cause: Inventory service DB migration locked tables for 8 minutes during peak traffic
investigation_steps: API gateway logs showed upstream timeout to inventory-service
inventory-service logs showed DB lock wait timeouts
DB admin logs confirmed ALTER TABLE migration running on products table
Migration had no timeout set and ran during business hours
resolution_steps: Confirm table lock: SELECT * FROM pg_locks WHERE NOT granted
Identify blocking query: SELECT pid, query, state FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE wait_event_type = 'Lock'
Kill the migration: SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) for the migration process
Verify 503s stop within 60 seconds of killing the lock
Reschedule migration for 2am maintenance window with statement_timeout set

title: Search service returning stale results — Elasticsearch index not updating
symptoms: Product search showing out-of-stock items as available, new products not appearing
root_cause: Elasticsearch sync worker OOM crashed silently, queue backed up with 180k events
investigation_steps: Search returning results from 6 hours ago based on index timestamps
Elasticsearch sync worker pod in CrashLoopBackOff
Worker OOM due to processing batch of 50000 products at once
Queue had 180000 pending update events backed up
resolution_steps: Check sync worker status: kubectl get pods -l app=es-sync-worker
Check queue depth: rabbitmq-admin queue-depth product-updates
Check worker logs for OOM: kubectl logs es-sync-worker --previous | tail -50
Restart worker with smaller batch: set BATCH_SIZE=1000 in worker config
Monitor queue drain — should process 180k events in about 40 minutes
Verify search index freshness after drain completes

title: Order service deadlock — concurrent checkout requests
symptoms: Random checkout failures, deadlock errors in order-service logs, orders stuck in pending
root_cause: Two concurrent checkouts acquiring row locks in opposite order causing deadlock
investigation_steps: order-service logs showed deadlock detected errors with transaction IDs
DB logs confirmed deadlock between transactions on orders and inventory tables
Code review showed checkout acquiring order lock then inventory lock
Refund flow acquiring inventory lock then order lock — opposite order
resolution_steps: Confirm active deadlocks: SELECT * FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE wait_event = 'relation'
Kill stuck transactions: SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) for deadlocked pids
Immediate relief clears pending orders — verify in orders table
Permanent fix: ensure all transactions acquire locks in same order (orders then inventory)
Add deadlock retry logic with exponential backoff in checkout service

title: SSL certificate expired — user-service HTTPS failing
symptoms: Users seeing SSL certificate error, all HTTPS requests to user-service rejected
root_cause: SSL certificate expired — auto-renewal cron job had been failing silently for 2 weeks
investigation_steps: Browser SSL error confirmed certificate expiry date was yesterday
Checked cert-manager logs — renewal job failing with DNS validation error
DNS TXT record for ACME challenge was deleted 2 weeks ago during DNS cleanup
Renewal had been silently failing, no alerting was configured
resolution_steps: Confirm expiry: openssl s_client -connect user-service.domain.com:443 | openssl x509 -noout -dates
Check cert-manager: kubectl logs -n cert-manager deployment/cert-manager | grep user-service
Re-add DNS TXT record for ACME challenge as shown in cert-manager logs
Trigger immediate renewal: kubectl annotate certificate user-service-tls cert-manager.io/issue-temporary-certificate=true
Verify new cert issued within 5 minutes and HTTPS restored
Add alerting for cert expiry 30 days in advance

title: Analytics pipeline failing — disk full on data processing node
symptoms: Analytics reports not updating, pipeline jobs failing with write errors
root_cause: Temp files from failed pipeline runs accumulated over 6 weeks, filled 500GB disk
investigation_steps: Pipeline logs showed No space left on device errors
df -h confirmed /data partition at 100% — 500GB full
du -sh /data/tmp showed 380GB of orphaned temp files from failed runs
Failed runs were not cleaning up temp files due to missing finally block
resolution_steps: Confirm disk usage: df -h /data and du -sh /data/tmp
Safe to delete temp files older than 24h: find /data/tmp -mtime +1 -delete
Verify disk drops below 80% after cleanup
Restart pipeline: systemctl restart analytics-pipeline
Add cleanup to pipeline code: use try/finally to always delete temp files
Add disk usage alerting at 75% threshold

title: Third-party payment gateway timeout — Stripe API unreachable
symptoms: All payments failing, Stripe API calls timing out after 30 seconds
root_cause: Stripe had a regional outage affecting their EU endpoints for 45 minutes
investigation_steps: payment-service logs showed Stripe API connection timeout on every request
Checked Stripe status page — confirmed EU region incident in progress
Internal infrastructure metrics all normal — not our issue
Fallback to US endpoint was disabled in config after previous cost optimisation
resolution_steps: Confirm Stripe outage: check https://status.stripe.com for active incidents
Check which endpoint is configured: grep STRIPE_API_URL in payment-service config
Enable US endpoint fallback: set STRIPE_FALLBACK_ENDPOINT=https://api.stripe.com in config
Restart payment-service to pick up new config
Monitor payment success rate — should recover immediately
Re-enable EU endpoint once Stripe resolves the incident

title: User service CPU spike — N+1 query on profile endpoint
symptoms: user-service CPU at 100%, /api/profile endpoint taking 15-30 seconds, timeouts
root_cause: New feature deployment introduced N+1 query — fetching user orders one by one in a loop
investigation_steps: CPU metrics showed spike starting exactly at v3.1.0 deployment time
Slow query log showed hundreds of SELECT queries per profile request
Each query fetching one order record — profile with 50 orders made 50 DB queries
Previous version made a single JOIN query — regression introduced in new feature
resolution_steps: Confirm N+1: enable query logging and hit /api/profile, count queries in logs
Check deployment time vs CPU spike: compare deployment timestamp with metrics
Quick fix: rollback to v3.0.9 to restore single JOIN query
Proper fix: rewrite profile endpoint to use SELECT * FROM orders WHERE user_id IN (...)
Add query count assertion in integration tests to prevent regression

title: Message queue consumer lag — email jobs not processing
symptoms: Transactional emails delayed by 2-4 hours, queue depth growing continuously
root_cause: Single consumer instance unable to keep up after 10x traffic spike from marketing campaign
investigation_steps: Queue monitoring showed consumer lag at 45000 messages and growing
email-service had only 1 consumer instance running
Marketing sent campaign email to 500k users triggering mass signups
Consumer processing at 50 msgs/sec, incoming at 500 msgs/sec
resolution_steps: Check queue depth: rabbitmq-admin list-queues name messages consumers
Check current consumer count and processing rate in email-service logs
Scale up consumers: kubectl scale deployment email-consumer --replicas=10
Monitor queue depth — should start decreasing within 2 minutes
Set up auto-scaling based on queue depth metric going forward

title: Auth service JWT secret rotation broke all sessions
symptoms: All logged-in users suddenly getting 401 errors, mass session expiry across platform
root_cause: JWT secret rotated in auth-service but other services still using old secret to verify tokens
investigation_steps: 401 errors spiked across all services simultaneously
auth-service logs showed successful token generation with new secret
api-gateway logs showed JWT signature verification failed on every request
Found secret rotation script only updated auth-service env, not dependent services
resolution_steps: Confirm JWT verification error: kubectl logs api-gateway | grep 'signature verification'
Check which secret each service is using: kubectl get secret jwt-secret -o yaml for each service
Update JWT secret in all dependent services: api-gateway, order-service, user-service
Rolling restart all services to pick up new secret
Verify 401s stop within 2 minutes of restarts completing
Update rotation runbook to include all dependent services

title: Inventory service slow — missing DB index on product lookup
symptoms: Product detail pages loading in 8-12 seconds, inventory-service response time degraded
root_cause: Full table scan on products table after new filtering feature deployed without adding index
investigation_steps: inventory-service p99 latency went from 120ms to 9000ms after v2.1.0 deploy
Slow query log showed sequential scan on products table taking 7-8 seconds
EXPLAIN ANALYZE confirmed full table scan on category_id column
New feature added WHERE category_id = ? filter but no index was created
resolution_steps: Confirm slow query: run EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT * FROM products WHERE category_id = 1
Check existing indexes: SELECT indexname FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename = 'products'
Add index concurrently to avoid locking: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_products_category ON products(category_id)
Verify query plan switches to index scan after creation
Monitor p99 latency — should return to under 150ms within minutes of index creation

title: Shipping service crash — unhandled null in address parser
symptoms: Shipping label generation failing for all international orders, 500 errors
root_cause: New address parser assuming state field always present — international addresses have no state
investigation_steps: shipping-service logs showed NullPointerException on address.state.toUpperCase()
Only international orders affected — domestic orders working fine
v1.5.0 deployed 3 hours ago added new address validation
New validation code assumed state field was always populated
resolution_steps: Confirm error in logs: kubectl logs shipping-service | grep NullPointerException | tail -20
Verify only international orders affected by checking order IDs in errors vs country codes
Immediate fix: rollback to v1.4.9 to restore international shipping
Proper fix: add null check — use address.state?.toUpperCase() or default to empty string
Add integration test with international address (no state field) before next deploy

title: Rate limiter blocking legitimate users — Redis counter overflow
symptoms: High-value customers getting 429 Too Many Requests despite normal usage
root_cause: Redis rate limit counter stored as 32-bit integer overflowed for accounts with high historical request counts
investigation_steps: 429 errors only affecting accounts created before 2022 with high usage
Rate limit counters in Redis showing negative values for affected accounts
Counter stored as Redis INCR which defaults to 64-bit but was cast to int32 in application code
Accounts with over 2.1 billion lifetime requests hit integer overflow
resolution_steps: Identify affected accounts: redis-cli SCAN with pattern ratelimit:* and find negative values
Immediate fix: redis-cli DEL ratelimit:user:{id} to reset counters for affected users
Verify affected users can make requests again within 60 seconds
Fix application code to use int64 for counter storage
Add monitoring for negative counter values as anomaly detection

title: Reporting service timeout — unoptimised aggregation query
symptoms: Monthly sales report generation timing out after 30 seconds, finance team unable to pull reports
root_cause: Report query doing aggregation over 18 months of un-indexed transaction data — 40M rows
investigation_steps: Report endpoint timing out at exactly 30 seconds — hitting query timeout
EXPLAIN ANALYZE showed sequential scan on transactions table — 40 million rows
No index on transaction_date column used in WHERE clause
Data volume has grown 3x in past 6 months making previously acceptable query too slow
resolution_steps: Confirm query timeout: check reporting-service logs for timeout errors with query details
Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the report query to see full scan cost
Add index: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_transactions_date ON transactions(transaction_date)
If index not sufficient, add monthly pre-aggregation table updated nightly
Increase query timeout temporarily to 120s while permanent fix is implemented

title: File upload service failing — S3 bucket permissions misconfigured
symptoms: Profile picture and document uploads failing with 403 errors, users cannot upload
root_cause: IAM policy update removed PutObject permission from upload-service role
investigation_steps: upload-service logs showed AccessDenied: s3:PutObject on every upload attempt
S3 bucket policy had not changed — issue was in IAM role policy
Infrastructure team ran IAM policy cleanup script 2 hours before incident
Script incorrectly removed PutObject from upload-service-role permissions
resolution_steps: Confirm IAM error: aws s3 cp test.txt s3://your-bucket/ using upload-service credentials
Check current IAM policy: aws iam get-role-policy --role-name upload-service-role
Add back PutObject permission to upload-service-role for the uploads bucket
Test upload immediately after policy update — takes effect within 60 seconds
Add IAM policy changes to change management process requiring approval

title: Recommendation engine cold start — model not loaded in memory
symptoms: Product recommendations returning empty, first request after deploy taking 45 seconds
root_cause: ML model loaded lazily on first request instead of at startup — cold start under load causes timeout
investigation_steps: First request after each deployment timing out for all users hitting that pod
recommendation-service logs showed model loading taking 42 seconds on first request
Model is 2.1GB and loaded from GCS on first predict() call
No readiness probe configured — traffic sent to pod before model loaded
resolution_steps: Confirm cold start: kubectl logs recommendation-service | grep 'Loading model'
Check readiness probe config: kubectl describe deployment recommendation-service
Immediate fix: kubectl rollout restart to trigger fresh load, then add readiness probe
Add startup model loading: move model.load() to service __init__ not first request
Configure readiness probe: httpGet /health only returns 200 after model is loaded
Consider model caching on persistent volume to speed up future restarts

title: Webhook delivery failures — TLS handshake error to partner endpoint
symptoms: Partner integration not receiving order events, webhook delivery failing since morning
root_cause: Partner updated their server to require TLS 1.3 but our webhook client only supports TLS 1.2
investigation_steps: webhook-service logs showed SSL handshake failure on delivery to partner endpoint
curl to partner endpoint confirmed TLS 1.3 required, 1.2 rejected
Partner sent email notification about TLS upgrade 2 weeks ago — not actioned
Webhook client library version was 2 years old with no TLS 1.3 support
resolution_steps: Confirm TLS issue: curl --tlsv1.2 https://partner-endpoint.com/webhook and check error
Check webhook client library version in requirements.txt
Update webhook client library to latest version with TLS 1.3 support
Deploy updated service and test webhook delivery to partner endpoint
Verify delivery success rate returns to 100% in webhook delivery logs
Set up process to review partner infrastructure change notifications

title: Session store unavailable — Memcached cluster failover failure
symptoms: Users being logged out randomly, session data lost intermittently
root_cause: Primary Memcached node failed but failover to replica failed due to misconfigured health check
investigation_steps: session-service logs showed connection refused to primary Memcached node
Memcached primary node had crashed due to OOM
Replica node was healthy but health check endpoint returned wrong status code
Failover logic checked for HTTP 200 but replica returned HTTP 204
resolution_steps: Check Memcached cluster status: memcached-tool primary:11211 stats
Manually trigger failover: update SESSION_STORE_HOST to point to replica
Restart session-service to connect to replica — sessions restore immediately
Fix health check: update failover logic to accept both 200 and 204 as healthy
Restart crashed primary node and restore as replica once stable
Add Memcached OOM alerting and increase memory allocation

title: CI/CD pipeline deploying broken build — test suite not running
symptoms: Production outage after deployment, unit tests would have caught the bug
root_cause: GitHub Actions workflow misconfiguration caused test job to be skipped on main branch merges
investigation_steps: Post-incident review showed regression that unit tests cover was deployed to production
Checked GitHub Actions run history — test job showed as skipped not passing
Workflow yaml had incorrect branch filter — tests only ran on PR branches not main
Change merged directly to main without PR bypassed test requirement
resolution_steps: Check workflow runs: review GitHub Actions history for recent main branch deployments
Identify skipped test jobs and which PRs bypassed the test requirement
Fix workflow: remove branch filter so tests run on all branches including main
Add branch protection rule requiring tests to pass before any merge to main
Rollback the broken deployment: kubectl rollout undo for affected service
Add required status checks in GitHub branch protection settings

title: Product images not loading — CDN cache poisoning
symptoms: Randomly serving wrong product images to users, some product pages showing competitor images
root_cause: CDN cache key did not include tenant ID — multi-tenant images cached and served across tenants
investigation_steps: Users reporting seeing wrong product images — images from different seller accounts
CDN logs showed cache hits serving image responses with wrong tenant IDs
Cache key was constructed using only image filename, not tenant_id/filename
Two tenants had products with same filename — cache collision serving wrong image
resolution_steps: Immediate: purge entire CDN image cache to stop wrong images being served
Confirm fix by requesting same filename for two different tenants — should get different images
Fix cache key: update CDN configuration to use tenant_id/image_filename as cache key
Purge cache again after config update to ensure clean state
Audit whether any user data was exposed and notify affected tenants
Add cache key validation to CDN deployment checklist

title: Database replica lag — read queries returning stale data
symptoms: Users seeing orders they just placed as missing, inventory counts inconsistent
root_cause: Read replica fell behind primary by 4 minutes due to long-running analytics query blocking replication
investigation_steps: order-service read queries routed to replica — replica was 4 minutes behind primary
Replica lag metric showed sudden spike from normal 50ms to 240 seconds
Analytics team ran large report query directly on replica — blocked replication thread
Replication slot held open while analytics query ran for 6 minutes
resolution_steps: Check replica lag: SELECT now() - pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp() AS replication_lag
Identify blocking queries: SELECT pid, query, state FROM pg_stat_activity ON replica
Kill analytics query blocking replication: SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid)
Monitor replica lag — should catch up to primary within 2-3 minutes after query killed
Route order-service reads to primary temporarily until replica is fully caught up
Move analytics queries to dedicated read replica, not application replica

title: API keys exposed in logs — security incident
symptoms: Security team detected API keys in application logs indexed by log aggregator
root_cause: Debug logging added in v2.0.1 logged full request headers including Authorization header
investigation_steps: Security scan flagged API key pattern in Elasticsearch log index
Logs showed Authorization: Bearer sk-live-... values in plain text
Traced to integration-service v2.0.1 — added verbose header logging for debugging
Debug logging was committed to main branch and deployed without security review
resolution_steps: Immediate: rotate all exposed API keys found in logs — treat as compromised
Disable verbose header logging: deploy integration-service v2.0.2 with debug logs removed
Purge affected log entries from Elasticsearch: delete documents containing key patterns
Audit log access to determine who could have seen the exposed keys
Add secret scanning to CI pipeline to catch credentials in logs before deploy
Require security review for any changes that touch logging or authentication code

title: Background job runner out of workers — job queue frozen
symptoms: Scheduled reports not running, data sync jobs delayed by hours, job queue not draining
root_cause: Worker processes leaked due to uncaught exception in job teardown, exhausting worker pool
investigation_steps: job-runner showed 0 available workers despite pool configured for 20
ps aux showed 20 zombie job-runner processes all stuck in cleanup phase
Logs showed uncaught exception in job_teardown() leaving processes hanging
Worker pool had no timeout or health check to reclaim stuck workers
resolution_steps: Check worker status: ps aux | grep job-runner to see zombie processes
Immediate relief: kill all job-runner processes and restart service to reclaim workers
Verify queue starts draining within 2 minutes of restart
Fix job_teardown(): wrap in try/except/finally to ensure worker always returns to pool
Add worker heartbeat timeout — reclaim any worker not reporting in for 60 seconds
Add worker availability monitoring with alert when available workers drops below 5

title: Checkout flow broken — feature flag service unavailable
symptoms: Checkout page not loading, errors in frontend logs about feature flag service timeout
root_cause: Feature flag service had no circuit breaker — when it went down it caused cascade failure in checkout
investigation_steps: Checkout errors started exactly when feature-flag-service pod crashed
Checkout code called feature flag service synchronously with no timeout
feature-flag-service crashed due to Redis connection failure — its own dependency
No circuit breaker or fallback defaults — whole checkout blocked on flag service response
resolution_steps: Immediate: restart feature-flag-service to restore checkout functionality
Verify checkout works within 60 seconds of feature-flag-service coming back up
Fix Redis connection handling in feature-flag-service to handle Redis being down
Add circuit breaker to checkout: if flag service unavailable, use hardcoded safe defaults
Add timeout of 500ms on all feature flag calls — never block user flow on flag service
Add feature-flag-service health to checkout dependency health check

title: Data pipeline duplicate records — idempotency key not enforced
symptoms: Duplicate transactions appearing in reports, customer accounts showing double charges
root_cause: Pipeline retry logic reprocessed events without checking idempotency keys after partial failure
investigation_steps: Finance team noticed transaction counts 2x higher than expected in daily report
data-pipeline logs showed batch reprocessed after a timeout — no idempotency check
Events table had no unique constraint on idempotency_key column
Retry ran full batch from checkpoint without checking what was already committed
resolution_steps: Identify duplicates: SELECT idempotency_key, COUNT(*) FROM transactions GROUP BY idempotency_key HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
Deduplicate: DELETE FROM transactions WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT MIN(id) FROM transactions GROUP BY idempotency_key)
Add unique constraint: ALTER TABLE transactions ADD CONSTRAINT unique_idempotency_key UNIQUE (idempotency_key)
Fix pipeline retry: check idempotency_key before inserting each record
Notify affected customers of duplicate charge and initiate refunds
Add duplicate detection monitoring — alert if same key appears more than once

title: Service mesh certificate rotation broke inter-service communication
symptoms: Multiple services unable to communicate, 503 errors on all inter-service calls
root_cause: Istio certificate rotation updated certs on 60% of pods but rotation script failed midway leaving mismatched certs
investigation_steps: All inter-service calls failing with certificate verify failed errors
Istio cert rotation script had run and partially completed before script error
60% of pods had new cert, 40% had old cert — mTLS verification failing between mismatched pods
Istio pilot logs showed certificate distribution errors on 12 specific pods
resolution_steps: Identify pods with old certs: istioctl proxy-status | grep STALE
Force cert rotation on remaining pods: istioctl proxy-config secret <pod> to check each
Restart pods with stale certs: kubectl rollout restart deployment for each affected service
Verify all pods show current cert in istioctl proxy-status
Confirm inter-service calls working: test with curl between services
Fix rotation script to be atomic — all or nothing, with rollback on partial failure

title: Search autocomplete slow — Elasticsearch heap pressure
symptoms: Search autocomplete taking 3-5 seconds instead of under 100ms, partial UI freezes
root_cause: Elasticsearch JVM heap at 95% causing frequent GC pauses, triggered by large aggregation query added to autocomplete
investigation_steps: Elasticsearch cluster health showed yellow — heap usage at 95% on primary shard nodes
GC logs showed stop-the-world GC pauses every 15-20 seconds
New autocomplete feature added terms aggregation returning top 10000 suggestions
Aggregation loading entire suggestion dataset into heap on every autocomplete keypress
resolution_steps: Check ES heap: GET /_nodes/stats/jvm via Elasticsearch API, look for heap_used_percent
Check GC pressure: GET /_nodes/stats/jvm and look at gc.collectors.old.collection_time_in_millis
Immediate relief: reduce aggregation size from 10000 to 20 in autocomplete query
Deploy reduced aggregation as hotfix — autocomplete quality unaffected for top results
Long term: use Elasticsearch completion suggester instead of terms aggregation
Increase ES heap allocation from 4GB to 8GB to give headroom

title: Kubernetes node NotReady — kubelet OOM on high pod density node
symptoms: Several pods evicted, services degraded, one cluster node showing NotReady status
root_cause: Kubelet process OOMKilled on node running 45 pods — node memory limits too low for pod density
investigation_steps: kubectl get nodes showed one node in NotReady state
kubectl describe node showed MemoryPressure condition true
Node had 45 pods scheduled — above recommended density for 8GB node
Kubelet process itself was OOMKilled by the kernel — node lost control plane communication
resolution_steps: Confirm node status: kubectl get nodes and kubectl describe node <node-name>
Check memory pressure events: kubectl describe node | grep -A5 MemoryPressure
Cordon node to prevent new pods scheduling: kubectl cordon <node-name>
Drain evictable pods: kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
SSH to node and restart kubelet: systemctl restart kubelet
Once node Ready, uncordon: kubectl uncordon <node-name>
Long term: reduce max pods per node or increase node memory from 8GB to 16GB
